findings.title: properties.txt can auto-execute an arbitrary AI class
findings.entry_point: A local properties.txt supplies HomeAI or VisitorAI (ApoSoccerProperties.java:29-36); alternatively, the desktop "load AI" chooser supplies a selected .class path (ApoSoccerGame.java:1212-1218).
findings.sink: ApoSoccerClassLoader.loadClass calls defineClass on the selected file bytes (ApoSoccerClassLoader.java:90-92), and getAI immediately calls Class.newInstance (ApoSoccerClassLoader.java:39-43).
findings.data_path: ApoSoccerGame.init calls loadProperties (ApoSoccerGame.java:593); loadProperties reads properties.txt and calls loadPlayer with the stored path (ApoSoccerGame.java:620-630); loadPlayer derives the class name and directory (ApoSoccerGame.java:1224-1232), constructs ApoSoccerClassLoader (ApoSoccerGame.java:1257-1259), then getAI loads, defines, and instantiates the bytes.
findings.attack_scenario: An attacker distributes a game/mod folder containing properties.txt with "HomeAI: Payload.class" and a malicious Payload.class. When the victim launches the desktop game from that folder, the class is instantiated during initialization; its static initializer or constructor executes with the game process's user permissions. A direct social-engineering variant asks the victim to choose the same file through "load Home AI".
findings.preconditions: Desktop mode; the malicious class and configuration are in the launch working directory, or the user explicitly chooses the class; bytecode is compatible with the victim JVM. Extending ApoSoccerAI avoids the later cast failure, although constructor code runs before that cast.
findings.validation_plan: Compile a Payload class extending ApoSoccerAI whose static initializer creates a harmless marker file. Put Payload.class and a properties.txt containing "HomeAI: Payload.class" in the launch directory, start ApoSoccerMain, and confirm the marker appears before any user interaction. Repeat through the load-AI chooser to confirm the second entry path.

findings.title: Desktop startup loads an unverified DLL from user.dir
findings.entry_point: A local file named AIMultiplexer.dll in the process working directory, whose path comes from user.dir (ApoSoccerGame.java:583-586 and ApoSoccerConstants.java:324).
findings.sink: ApoSoccerAIJNI.loadMultiplexer passes that path directly to System.load (ApoSoccerAIJNI.java:7-9).
findings.data_path: ApoSoccerGame.init enters its desktop branch, concatenates System.getProperty("user.dir"), File.separator, and AIMultiplexer.dll, and calls loadMultiplexer (ApoSoccerGame.java:583-586); loadMultiplexer invokes System.load. The same feature also forwards chooser/properties-selected .dll or .so paths to the native loadAI method (ApoSoccerGame.java:1269-1274; ApoSoccerAIJNI.java:18-23).
findings.attack_scenario: An attacker places or replaces AIMultiplexer.dll in a writable game launch directory, for example in a repackaged game archive. The victim starts ApoSoccer; Windows loads the attacker's DLL before the menu appears, executing its native initialization code with the victim's permissions.
findings.preconditions: Desktop Windows deployment; the victim launches from a directory the attacker could populate or replace; the DLL matches the process architecture. For the secondary AI-DLL route, a legitimate multiplexer must first load.
findings.validation_plan: Build a same-architecture test DLL whose DllMain or JNI_OnLoad writes a harmless marker, name it AIMultiplexer.dll, place it in a disposable launch directory, and start ApoSoccerMain from that directory. The marker appearing during ApoSoccerGame.init proves the startup path. Separately select a marker AI DLL to test the native loadAI route.

findings.title: Replay track counts can crash playback or exhaust memory
findings.entry_point: A user-selected, attacker-crafted .rep file reaches ApoSoccerReplay.loadReplay through the visible "replay load" button (ApoSoccerGame.java:363-369 and 889-892; ApoSoccerReplay.java:234-239).
findings.sink: Playback bounds curStep only against the ball list (ApoSoccerReplay.java:308-310) and then indexes every independently sized player list with point.get(curStep) (ApoSoccerReplay.java:313-323 and 339-341).
findings.data_path: The chooser path is passed to ApoSoccerReplayIO.readLevel (ApoSoccerReplay.java:235-238); readLevel reads nine independently attacker-sized tracks (ApoSoccerReplayIO.java:48-62); readPlayer accepts each signed count without a range or cross-track equality check (ApoSoccerReplayIO.java:112-120); replay play enters playStep via ApoSoccerGame.thinkGame (ApoSoccerGame.java:1760-1765).
findings.attack_scenario: An attacker shares a syntactically complete replay with one ball point but zero points in each player track. The victim loads it and presses replay play. The ball-size guard passes at step zero, the first empty player list is indexed, and an uncaught IndexOutOfBoundsException terminates the game loop. A large positive count with enough coordinate bytes also creates unbounded ApoFloatPoint objects and can exhaust the heap.
findings.preconditions: Desktop mode; the victim chooses the malicious .rep and starts playback. The small crash case needs only valid modified-UTF team names, ball count 1 with one x/y pair, and count 0 for each of the eight player tracks.
findings.validation_plan: Create a binary replay using DataOutputStream: writeUTF("H"), writeUTF("V"), writeInt(1), two floats for the ball, then writeInt(0) eight times. Load it with "replay load", press "replay play", and confirm an IndexOutOfBoundsException at ApoSoccerReplay.setEntityPosition line 340 and cessation of the ApoThread loop. For memory impact, repeat under -Xmx128m with a large count and matching float pairs.

findings.title: Applet team artwork is fetched over plaintext HTTP
findings.entry_point: Image bytes returned by the fixed http://apo-games.de/apoSoccer/player/ team-asset locations used in applet mode (ApoSoccerGame.java:271-288 and 1051-1147).
findings.sink: ApoImage.getImage gives the unauthenticated URL response directly to ImageIO.read with no TLS, integrity check, size limit, or connection/read timeout (ApoImage.java:78-113).
findings.data_path: ApoAppletBufferedStrategy.init sets B_APPLET (ApoAppletBufferedStrategy.java:28-33); ApoSoccerGame assigns an http:// base when setting each AI (ApoSoccerGame.java:271-288); ApoTeam prefixes AI-provided emblem/player filenames with that base (ApoTeam.java:354-379); setAi or makeBackgroundWithEmblem requests the image (ApoTeam.java:279-284; ApoSoccerGame.java:738-753); ApoImage opens the URL.
findings.attack_scenario: A network attacker intercepts the plaintext asset request and returns a different valid image, changing team/player artwork shown by the client. The attacker can instead delay the response or return an image with extreme decoded dimensions to stall or exhaust the game. This path does not expose a score-submission or credential channel in this variant.
findings.preconditions: A legacy Java applet deployment is actually used, the selected AI returns a non-null emblem or custom player-image filename, and the attacker can intercept traffic to apo-games.de. The built-in AI implementations are not present in this source root, so their exact returned filenames could not be verified here.
findings.validation_plan: Run the applet path or a harness with B_APPLET=true and an ApoSoccerAI whose getEmblem returns "emblem.png" under the game's fixed HTTP base. Intercept apo-games.de with a controlled proxy or DNS mapping, return a visibly different PNG, and confirm both the plaintext request and substituted emblem. A delayed response can confirm the synchronous no-timeout stall.

findings.title: Dormant applet loader defines classes from arbitrary URL bytes
findings.code_excerpt:
byte b[] = loadClassData(name);
			c = defineClass(b, 0, b.length);
findings.entry_point: There is no source-visible untrusted entry point in the shipped applet flow. The primitive would receive a caller-supplied path and class name through the public ApoSoccerGame.loadPlayer overload (ApoSoccerGame.java:1253-1264).
findings.sink: ApoSoccerClassLoaderURL downloads name + ".class" through URLConnection (ApoSoccerClassLoaderURL.java:75-102), calls defineClass (line 64), then Class.newInstance (lines 21-29).
findings.data_path: The theoretical path is caller-controlled loadPlayer(path, classname, ".class") while B_APPLET is true (ApoSoccerGame.java:1253-1264) -> ApoSoccerClassLoaderURL.getAI -> loadClass -> loadClassData -> URLConnection.getInputStream (ApoSoccerClassLoaderURL.java:81-94) -> defineClass -> newInstance. Shipped applet buttons switch among already-linked AI objects through loadAI instead (ApoSoccerGame.java:923-946 and 1047-1149), while chooser and properties loading are disabled in applet mode (ApoSoccerGame.java:166-171 and 620-624).
findings.attack_scenario: Theoretical only: if an embedding layer or future caller exposes the public loadPlayer parameters to untrusted input, an attacker supplies an HTTP base URL and a class name, serves a malicious compatible .class, and obtains code execution within the applet's Java protection domain. No such caller is present in the reviewed source.
findings.preconditions: A non-shipped caller must invoke the public method with attacker-controlled values while B_APPLET is true; the runtime must permit the network connection and class definition; useful impact remains subject to the legacy applet sandbox/protection domain.
findings.validation_plan: For the primitive, serve a Payload.class extending ApoSoccerAI from a local HTTP server, set B_APPLET=true in a test harness, call loadPlayer with that base URL and class name, and observe a harmless static-initializer marker. Separately retain the call-site search showing that normal applet UI paths call loadAI, not loadPlayer, to confirm current non-reachability.

notes: All 77 Java files were pattern-scanned and 39 security-relevant or supporting files were opened directly. The tree contains imports for built-in AI classes at ApoSoccerGame.java:32-39 and only a native declaration for the AI-library loader at ApoSoccerAIJNI.java:18-23; those implementations are absent, which limits confirmation of their asset names and native ABI. The shared ApoIO URL read/write methods (org/apogames/ApoIO.java:135-145, 157-174, and 209-224), shared org.apogames.help.ApoClassLoader (ApoClassLoader.java:62-75), and ApoCopy file helpers (ApoCopy.java:27-73) have no source-visible subclass or call site in ApoSoccer, so they were not reported as reachable findings. No apo-games PHP/highscore endpoint, ObjectInputStream/ObjectOutputStream, MessageDigest/MD5, embedded credential, or authoritative server-side score flow appears in this variant.
